title: How Ruben Hassid built a multi-million LinkedIn AI education business as a solo creator
summary: Ruben Hassid explains how he went from a failed music label to a $3-4M/year business by writing "IKEA instructions" for AI tools on LinkedIn. He covers sponsorship terms, riding platform pushes, content-first positioning, the human edge against AI, and handling haters and burnout. (Interview in French; quotes translated.)

principles.text: Be useful by writing step-by-step how-tos; give instructions anyone can follow rather than selling yourself.
principles.quote: I often say that I'm kind of writing the IKEA instructions for AI tools. (translated from French)

principles.text: Turn audience demand into content: log every question from comments and DMs, then answer the most requested for free.
principles.quote: I look at all the comments, all the private messages, and I look at where people ask me for things the most. (translated from French)

principles.text: Sponsored content works when you keep creative control and only back tools you believe are best. Integrity builds audience trust.
principles.quote: If I don't like your tool, if I think there's a better tool to do that, to do the task, I'm not going to promote it. (translated from French)

principles.text: Structure creator deals around guaranteed reach: commit to a minimum number of views and post more if it's missed.
principles.quote: There's a minimum number of views I'll deliver. And if I don't hit that minimum, I commit to doing more posts on it. (translated from French)

principles.text: When a platform pushes a new format, ride it hard but briefly. What works stops working once the push ends.
principles.quote: Something that works stops working after a while. (translated from French)

principles.text: Price sponsorships on the buyer's value: ask whether LinkedIn is a major channel and whether those users have high LTV before quoting.
principles.quote: Are you sure that your LTV, the value of your users, is very high when people come from LinkedIn, and is LinkedIn a big channel for you? (translated from French)
